subject: Latency surge — consolidated impact matrix and guardrails declaration
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@finpay.com>, FinPay SRE <ops@finpay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Latency surge — consolidated impact matrix and guardrails declaration

Hi Peter / FinPay SRE team,

We detected a sustained latency surge affecting token-level inference for a subset of your traffic between 08:48–09:05 PT this morning. Early triage indicates higher-than-normal tokenizer cache thrashing combined with scheduling backpressure on a small pool of GPUs.

High-level:
- Scope: ~6% of requests routed to the west-us cluster; 1200 requests affected, peak 2.1s p90 token latency (typical ~0.35s).
- User-visible: transient token delays and partial streaming pauses; no permanent failures or data loss observed.
- Immediate mitigation applied (09:10 PT): temporary routing of affected prefix to warm cache pool + transient request shedding for non-critical long-horizon prompts.

We've attached a consolidated timeline and an impact matrix (timeline.csv, impact-matrix.xlsx) and will share kernel-level dumps for your SRE review (kernel-dump.txt). A short patch to introduce a per-worker circuit-breaker and conservative caching guardrails is included (guardrails-patch.diff).

Requested next steps from our side:
1) Joint 30-minute technical review at 11:00 PT today (I propose) — confirmed availability?
2) We will share a concise RCA note after the technical review and a proposed validation plan.
3) If you want immediate rollback of any specific config, let us know — we can revert routing to the warm pool or pin older tokenizer variant.

Apologies for the disruption; we are treating this with high priority.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
attachments: timeline.csv (csv), impact-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), kernel-dump.txt (log), guardrails-patch.diff (patch)

Date: 2026-11-30T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency surge — consolidated impact matrix and guardrails declaration

Peter — quick answers up front:
- Data exposure: none detected. The issue is strictly performance-related; there is no sign of exfiltration or unauthorized access. We have run request/response checks and validated logs for abnormal outbound events.
- Models: traffic hit both rwd-open-llama-13B and rwd-opt-6.7B tokenizer stacks where shared cache eviction patterns aligned poorly with our new scheduler micro-optimizations (rolled last week). The tokenizer variant mismatch is the primary vector.

Attached is a concise timeline excerpt (see timeline.csv) — key timestamps:
- 08:48 PT: first token delay detection by auto-alerts (p90 jump)
- 08:50 PT: elevated KV cache eviction rates observed on host pool w-3
- 08:55 PT: routing policy applied to divert 40% of affected prefixes to warm pool
- 09:10 PT: circuit-breaker patch staged as emergency config (reduced p90 by ~60%)
- 09:20 PT: full mitigation in place; monitoring resumed to normal baseline by 09:35 PT

Proposed cadence for the technical review: 11:00 PT today (30 min). If your team prefers 13:00 PT, we can accommodate — please confirm. We'll also provide a short validation checklist post-call you can run against a representative prefix.

Thanks,
Grace
attachments: timeline.csv (csv), impact-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@finpay.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Technical addendum — root cause hypothesis & guardrails (notes for call)

Hi all — brief technical note ahead of the 11:00 PT review. I'll present this during the call but wanted to leave a written copy for the SRE team.

Root cause (summary):
- Regression introduced in scheduler micro-optimization v2.3.1 altered request batching distribution. Under a specific request-length distribution we observed thrash in the tokenizer KV cache leading to frequent cache eviction and rehydrate cycles. The rehydrates triggered expensive kernel context switches on a subset of GPUs which amplified tail latency.

Why this reached customer traffic:
- The new scheduler was rolled to a warm-but-not-canary pool last week to increase throughput; the traffic profile that surfaces the regression overlapped with FinPay's long-horizon prompts and an uncommon tokenization pattern.

Mitigations applied (short-term):
1) Immediate routing to warm cache pool + conservative request shedding for unusually long prompts.
2) Emergency circuit-breaker limiting in-flight tokenizer rehydrates per-worker (guardrails-patch.diff).
3) Rollback candidate prepared: revert scheduler to v2.3.0 for the 4 hosts in pool w-3 if we observe recurrence.

Planned medium-term fixes:
- Add deterministic synthetic workload tests for tokenization cache stress to CI.
- Introduce a tokenization cache telemetry export (per-prefix eviction rates) and dashboard.
- Harden canary rollout rules to require cross-traffic-profile validation before pool-wide rollouts.

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- Repeatable reproduction test fails under current conditions in staging but passes with guardrails enabled.
- FinPay validation run (we'll provide checklist) shows no p90 > 2.0s across representative prefixes for 2 hours.

Attachments referenced: guardrails-patch.diff (shows circuit-breaker), kernel-dump.txt (host w-3 snapshot).

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@finpay.com>, FinPay SRE <ops@finpay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: consolidated impact, agreed actions, and validation checklist

Peter / team — thanks for joining the call. Short summary and explicit actions we've agreed on:

What happened (TL;DR): a scheduler micro-optimization caused tokenizer cache eviction thrash under your traffic profile; tail latency rose temporarily. No data exposure.

Agreed immediate actions (owner / ETA):
- Redwood: deploy guardrails-patch.diff to all west-us warm pool hosts (Hannah) — complete by 17:00 PT today.
- Redwood: run 2-hour validation in staging and share synthetic reproduction logs (Marcus) — deliver by 09:00 PT tomorrow.
- FinPay: run acceptance checklist on 3 representative prefixes; confirm no p90 > 2.0s for 2 hours (Peter/ops) — target window 09:30–11:30 PT tomorrow.
- Joint: if FinPay validation fails, we will revert scheduler to v2.3.0 on the affected hosts and schedule a deeper postmortem within 72 hours (Grace).

Acceptance criteria and verification:
- No p90 token latency > 2.0s for the agreed prefixes during the 2-hour run.
- No increase in tokenization cache eviction rates above baseline in exported telemetry.

Attachments & references: timeline.csv, impact-matrix.xlsx, kernel-dump.txt, guardrails-patch.diff; ticket OPS-6789 in our tracker; joint notes in Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d_guardrails_doc

We'll follow up with a short written RCA within 48 hours and a permanent mitigations roadmap. Thank you for the partnership and for validating the checklist as soon as you can.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
